```{r, message=F, warning=F}

cutoffs <- c(2.5, 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5)

# Count rows greater than or equal to each cutoff
broad_peaks_counts <- sapply(cutoffs, function(x) sum(broad_peaks$fold_enrichment >= x, na.rm = TRUE))
narrow_peaks_counts=sapply(cutoffs, function(x) sum(narrow_peaks$fold_enrichment >= x, na.rm = TRUE))

```




```{r, message=F, warning=F}
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# 1. Create the data frame
cutoffs <- c("2.5", "5", "7.5", "10", "12.5")
df <- data.frame(
  Cutoff = rep(factor(cutoffs, levels = cutoffs), 2),
  Counts = c(broad_peaks_counts, narrow_peaks_counts),
  Type   = rep(c("Broad Peaks", "Narrow Peaks"), each = 5)
)

# 2. Create the plot with a linear Y-axis
ggplot(df, aes(x = Cutoff, y = Counts, fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(Counts)), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
            vjust = -0.5, 
            size = 3.2, 
            fontface = "bold") +
  # Expand upper limit by 15% to ensure the "28,372" text doesn't get clipped
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Broad Peaks" = "#0073C2FF", "Narrow Peaks" = "#EFC000FF")) +
  labs(
    x = "Fold Enrichment Cutoff",
    y = "Number of Peaks",
    fill = "Peak Type",
    title = "Peak Counts by Fold Enrichment Cutoff"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

```
